title: evidence-request-list
description: Provided-by-client (PBC) evidence request list for a single control test cycle. One row per evidence ask, with control-objective tie, criterion source, artifact description, format requested, system of record, owner role, due date, population reference, reliance classification, and status. Produced before fieldwork begins; tracked through fieldwork; closed when all rows resolve to received-or-not-applicable. Downstream consumers: workpaper-drafter (reads request_id per evidence row in the workpaper's evidence-inspected table); evidence-binder (reads the closed list as the index of what was produced for this cycle). The list is the operational ask; conclusions live in the workpaper.

request_list_id.description: Stable identifier per firm naming convention.

test_id.description: Foreign key into test-plan-builder output. Identifies the test plan this request list serves.

control_id.description: Firm control register ID for the control under test.

obligation_ids.description: Firm obligation register IDs the control addresses.

engagement_id.description: Optional pointer to the engagement-scope record under which this request list was produced.

period_start.description: First day of the period the requests address.

period_end.description: Last day of the period the requests address.

business_unit.description: Business unit owning the control. Role-level, not individual-level.

scope_statement.description: Two to three sentences. What the request list covers, what is in and out of scope, what triggered the cycle.

source_posture.description: Source posture the testing operates under. Public-only request lists do not ask for firm-system extracts.

role.description: Preparer role, not individual name. Examples: compliance-testing analyst, internal-audit senior.

reviewer.description: Reviewer must be a separate role from preparer. Reviewer signs the request list before it is fielded; fielding requests before sign-off is a methodology weakness.

escalation_path.description: Named escalation path for overdue or contested requests. Role-level, not individual-level. Example: testing manager, then chief compliance officer; control-owner manager for unresponsive owners.

request_summary.description: Aggregate counts derived from the requests array. Recomputed on revision.

requests.description: One row per evidence ask. Specific, fulfillable without follow-up call.

request_id.description: Stable per request, e.g., R001. Carried into the workpaper's evidence-inspected table and the closure binder.

control_objective.description: What the evidence supports. Tied to a procedure in the test plan, not free-form.

criterion_source.description: Single named source: regulator + instrument + section, policy + section, or methodology. One source per row; if the criterion stack is complex, split the request.

artifact_description.description: The specific artifact requested. Specific enough that a reasonable owner can fulfill without follow-up call. Not 'all relevant documents'.

format_requested.description: Format the request expects. CSV asks should name expected columns in artifact_description.

system_of_record.description: Named system or report from which the artifact comes. 'Internal database' does not pass; name the system.

owner_role.description: Role responsible for fulfillment, not individual name.

population_reference.description: Sample ID set, full-population pointer, or stratum. Ties the request to the sampling memo when one exists.

reliance_classification.description: Drives the workpaper's reliability assessment. Vendor and management-prepared evidence trigger separate completeness-and-accuracy checks.

sensitivity.description: Set honestly. NPI, PHI, PCI, SAR content, and customer narratives carry confidential or restricted, not the internal default. Drives downstream handling and routing.

status.description: Operational status. Updated through fieldwork. Closed when received in usable form or formally not-applicable.

received_date.description: Filled when status moves to received or received-partial.

received_evidence_id.description: Stable evidence ID assigned on receipt. Carried into the workpaper's evidence-inspected table and the closure binder.

re_ask_count.description: Count of times the request had to be re-asked. High counts surface fielding problems.

notes.description: Free-text notes on the request. Avoid restating fields; use for clarifications, partial-receipt commentary, or deferral rationale.

not_applicable_items.description: Items intentionally not requested with rationale. Avoids re-ask in the next cycle and documents the boundary.

rationale.description: Why this item is not in scope (out of period, separate test, separate population stratum, separate cycle, restricted access).

covered_by_test_id.description: Test ID where this item is covered, when it sits in another cycle's scope.

limitations.description: What the request list does not cover; reliance posture; access constraints.

downstream_consumers.description: Skills that consume this list. Naming the consumers makes the lifecycle visible at planning time.

reviewer_questions.description: Questions for the named reviewer to consider before pre-fielding sign-off.

confidence_label.description: Reflects source posture, criteria maturity, and any open question on the request set. Per references/review-gates.md.

human_review_required.description: Always true. Pre-fielding sign-off is a hard gate; fielding requests before reviewer sign-off is a methodology weakness.

review_gates.description: Named human-review gates this list must clear. Drawn from references/review-gates.md.

source_trace.description: Citations supporting material claims in the list (criteria sources, format conventions, named-not-applicable rationales).
